name: I/O Module
description: A plug-in module with a low-voltage sensor input and a relay output. It connects alarm sensors, door strikes, garage door openers, and other contact-closure devices to an Insteon network.

productKeyVerification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives the IOLinc [2450] 0x00001A. The identity's observation saw no key because ID Request's reply, a SET Button Pressed broadcast, carries none; Product Data Request, which carries it, wasn't recorded.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: ID Request answered with category 0x07, subcategory 0x00 and firmware 0x41, and no product key was reported. Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) answered with cmd2 0x02, i2CS, as the catalog's engine entry gives. A Hub 2245, with modem firmware 0xA5, kept 0x01 0x00 0x41 as Data 1 to 3 of its controller record for the device in group 0, as it did for other devices: Data 3 there is the firmware, and Data 1 isn't the category.
Read from the 0x07/0x00 version: 0x07/0x0D is the version that detects 50 or 60 Hz power, which Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) lists as model 2450, and no document gives it other commands.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: linked to a Hub 2245, the device wrote its controller record for group 1, to the Hub, with Data 1 to 3 as 0x03 0x00 0x00. Tapping its SET button sent a group 1 broadcast, Light On (cmd1 0x11), then an ALL-Link cleanup to the Hub. The sensor input itself wasn't changed, so its messages weren't seen; neither the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual nor the I/O Linc command set gives the input's group number.

steps.text: Plug the I/O Module into an unswitched outlet near the sensor.
If using a sensor, connect one of its leads to the Ground terminal and the other to the Sense terminal, or use the 3.5 mm sensor jack.
steps.expect: Green sensor status LED turns on and off as the sensor closes and opens

steps.text: If using the output relay, set up the relay mode and links before connecting the device to the relay terminals (N/C, N/O, COM).

notes: Sensor wire of 16 to 28 gauge fits; 20 to 22 gauge is recommended.
The 5V terminal supplies 5 V at 10 mA if needed. Applying more than 5 V can damage the sensor input.
Normally Closed and Common are connected when the relay is closed; Normally Open and Common are connected when it is open.
Don't plug it into a switched outlet, a filtered power strip or an AC filter, and don't stack Insteon devices in each other's pass-through outlets.

steps.text: Put the sensor in the state that should send an on command.
steps.expect: Sensor status LED on if the sensor is closed, off if open

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the I/O Module beeps, about 3 seconds.

notes: As controller (sensor input): after these steps press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds; the I/O Module's status LED stops blinking and stays on. The opposite sensor state sends off. Tapping the SET button also triggers the linked responders.

As responder (output relay, latching mode): tap the SET button to set the relay to the state an on command should give (LED dim when open, bright when closed), put the controller in linking mode, then press and hold the I/O Module's SET button until it beeps (3 seconds). Momentary modes A, B and C have their own variations in the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual.
The linking steps for the relay assume the default latching mode; set the relay mode after linking.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the I/O Module beeps, about 3 seconds.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.

Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: To link the relay to a group of the Hub's own, set the relay first to the state the Hub's On should give (On, cmd1 0x11, or Off, cmd1 0x13): a link to the relay records its state when it's made.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: with a Hub 2245's modem already in Start ALL-Linking as controller, holding the SET button for about 3 seconds linked the Hub as its controller. The modem had to be in linking mode before the hold; a hold made before the modem started linking wasn't seen.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: once the device had been linked so, linking it again by its Insteon ID worked for both links with no SET button press: the extended Enter Linking Mode with the modem in Start ALL-Linking as controller of group 0, then Enter Linking Mode for group 1 with the modem in Start ALL-Linking as responder.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: the device wrote its responder record for the Hub's group 0 with Data 1 to 3 as 0x00 0x00 0x00, and its controller record for group 1 as the profile's group gives. Linked again after both links had been removed, it wrote the two records again at other free ALL-Link database addresses.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub. Neither the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual nor the I/O Linc command set gives the sensor input's group number; group 1 is the one a device used, as the profile's group records.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: with a Hub 2245's modem in Start ALL-Linking as the controller of group 0, the device linked as its responder both from its SET button and from the extended Enter Linking Mode with cmd2 0x01.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: with a Hub 2245's modem in Start ALL-Linking as the responder, Enter Linking Mode with cmd2 0x01 linked the device as the controller of group 1, and it wrote its controller record for group 1.

The Insteon Developer's Guide (2009) says i1 devices don't support Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), and the catalog doesn't know the engine of every version of this product. An i2 or i2CS version takes it; ask the device with Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) first. Seen on a device running firmware 0x41, an i2CS version: the extended Enter Linking Mode put it in linking mode for both legs.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the I/O Module beeps, about 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps, about 3 seconds.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds within 4 minutes; the status LED stops blinking and stays on.

To unlink the I/O Module from a controller, put the controller in unlinking mode and press and hold the I/O Module's SET button until it beeps (3 seconds); the status LED turns off for about 1 second and back on.

steps.text: Unlink the I/O Module from any controllers.
Unplug the I/O Module.
Wait about 10 seconds.
While holding down the SET button, plug it back in.
Keep holding the SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes once and turns off for a few seconds, then beeps as the LED turns back on

notes: Clears all Insteon links and X10 addresses, disables sensor control of the relay, returns the relay to latching mode and sets the momentary duration back to 2 seconds.

steps.text: Unlink the I/O Module from every controller it is linked to.

notes: Otherwise controllers keep retrying commands and slow the system.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
If the Hub also controls the I/O Linc's relay from a group of its own, have the Hub start unlinking for that group (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
If so, have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
If so, wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: with a Hub 2245's modem, these steps removed both links with no SET button press: Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) for group 1, with the modem joining as responder, then Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF and Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) for the modem's group 0.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: after these steps the device still answered ID Request and Get Insteon Engine Version, because it still held responder records for the same Hub in groups other than 0 and 1, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. Unlinking by the modem's own records leaves the device's records for groups the modem has no record of.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, Enter Linking Mode and Enter Unlinking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub. Neither the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual nor the I/O Linc command set gives the sensor input's group number; group 1 is the one a device used, as the profile's group records.

notes: 0x07/0x0D is the version that detects 50 or 60 Hz power; Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) lists it as model 2450, and HouseLinc as 2450-50-60.

Inferred: group 1 is both the sensor, which controls it, and the output relay, which responds to it. The I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual says the output relay responds to Insteon ON and OFF commands, and the ioLinc command set's relay commands, Light ON (cmd1 0x11) and Light OFF (cmd1 0x13) sent to the device directly, are read from that and the Insteon Developer's Guide; no document gives the I/O Linc's direct commands.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)
